skill.name: vibecoder-guide-legacy
skill.description: Helps nontechnical builders use natural-language prompts to get simple next-step guidance during coding workflows.
skill.summary: Guides beginner coding-agent users through project status, next actions, and common blockers.
skill.author: Chachamaru127

security_audit.summary: Static command execution and obfuscation alerts were false positives after reviewing SKILL.md. The flagged backticks are Markdown inline code around a task marker, and the file is readable Markdown content rather than binary or encrypted material.

static_findings.snippet: 3. **現在のタスク状態** → `cc:WIP` マーカーの有無

static_findings.pattern: [HEURISTIC] High file entropy (6.76 bits) - possible binary/encrypted content

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 126 uses Markdown inline-code backticks around the literal marker cc:WIP. It does not execute a shell command or instruct the agent to run external commands.
SKILL.md is readable Markdown with YAML front matter and Japanese text. No binary, encrypted, or hidden content was found in the reviewed file.

content.value_statement: Nontechnical builders can lose momentum when a coding agent asks for next steps. This skill gives simple prompts and context-aware guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Recognizes help-oriented phrases in Japanese and English.
Explains next steps for users who lack technical workflow knowledge.
Provides response patterns for project start, active work, phase completion, and errors.
Uses AGENTS.md, Plans.md, cc:WIP, and recent errors as context signals.
Limits its declared tool access to Read.
limitations: It is marked as deprecated and superseded by vibecoder-guide.
It provides guidance text and does not implement features by itself.
It depends on project files such as AGENTS.md and Plans.md being available.

use_cases.title: Start a New Project
use_cases.description: Help a beginner describe an app idea and choose the first practical action.

use_cases.title: Continue Existing Work
use_cases.description: Explain whether to start a plan, continue a task, test progress, or review code.

use_cases.title: Recover From Confusion
use_cases.description: Translate errors or stalled progress into clear choices such as fix, explain, or skip.

prompt_templates.title: Ask What To Do Next
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user needs a simple next action.
prompt_templates.prompt: What should I do next in this project? Explain the answer in simple language.

prompt_templates.title: Start From An Idea
prompt_templates.scenario: User has an idea but no technical plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to build a small task management app. Help me begin with natural language steps.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Progress
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants status before choosing the next task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Look at the current project context and tell me whether I should continue, test, review, or plan.

prompt_templates.title: Recover From A Blocker
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user wants context-aware options after an error.
prompt_templates.prompt: An error happened during the current task. Summarize the situation and give clear options for fixing, explaining, or skipping it.

output_examples.output: You have a plan, but no active task. Start with the first phase or ask to review the plan.

output_examples.input: I am stuck after an error.
output_examples.output: The skill would explain the issue in plain language and offer choices to fix it, explain it, or move on.

output_examples.input: I want to build a portfolio site.
output_examples.output: The skill would help turn the idea into a first project step and suggest simple phrases to continue.

best_practices: Use short natural-language requests when asking for next steps.
Keep project planning files current so context checks stay useful.
Prefer the newer vibecoder-guide skill when available.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for direct implementation instructions.
Do not rely on it for deep technical code review.
Do not expect it to replace project planning or testing.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for nontechnical users who want simple guidance while using coding agents.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It guides the conversation and suggests next actions.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Why is it called legacy?
faq.answer: Its metadata marks it as deprecated and superseded by vibecoder-guide.

faq.question: Does it work in Japanese?
faq.answer: Yes. The source content focuses on Japanese beginner prompts and also includes English help phrases.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. Its declared allowed tool is Read, and the reviewed content does not contain command execution instructions.
